hints: Focus on what Fehling's reagent actually tests for, it only gives a brick-red precipitate with one type of carbonyl group.
That test immediately narrows you to two structures, both aldehydes with a -CHO group, while the two ketones can be ruled out.
Now check for stereoisomerism by looking for a chiral carbon with four different groups or a C=C that can show cis-trans isomerism.
walkthrough:
**Use Fehling's Test To Find The Functional Group**

Fehling's reagent is warmed with a carbonyl compound to distinguish aldehydes from ketones. Only aldehydes are oxidised and give the brick-red precipitate of $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$.

Rule:
$$\text{R-CHO + Fehling's (warmed) -> brick-red precipitate, R-CO-R' -> no reaction}$$

**Sort The Four Structures Into Aldehydes And Ketones**

Look at the $\text{C=O}$ position. Structures A and D end in $-\text{CHO}$, so they are aldehydes and give a positive test. Structures B and C have $\text{C=O}$ in the middle, so they are ketones and give no precipitate.

**Test The Aldehydes For Stereoisomers**

Structure A is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=CH-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$. Its $\text{C=C}$ has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups on one carbon, so no cis-trans isomerism, and it has no chiral centre.

Structure D is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CHO}$, which is 2-methylpentanal. Carbon 2 is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CHO}$, four different groups, so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism.

**Conclude The Structure**

Only the chiral aldehyde satisfies both conditions at once, positive Fehling's test plus stereoisomers. That is the structure with a branched aldehyde chain.

options.A: This is 4-methylpent-3-enal, an aldehyde, so it does give a precipitate with Fehling's. However it has no stereoisomers because the C=C has two identical methyl groups on one end, so cis-trans is impossible, and there is no chiral centre.
options.B: This is hex-4-en-2-one, a ketone, so it gives no reaction with Fehling's reagent. Although its C=C can show cis-trans (E/Z) isomerism, it fails the first condition.
options.C: This is 3-methylpentan-2-one, a ketone, so it gives no reaction with Fehling's reagent. Although carbon 3 is chiral and gives optical isomers, it fails the Fehling's condition.
options.D: This is 2-methylpentanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO}$. As an aldehyde it is oxidised on warming with Fehling's to give the brick-red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate. Carbon 2 is a chiral centre with four different groups, so it exists as a pair of optical stereoisomers.
